bmr: BMR and bundled BM++ temporal kernels
R package version and GPL>=2 declaration; RcppArmadillo dependency.
Build selects RcppArmadillo, BLAS/LAPACK and disabled Armadillo debug checks; runtime equivalence not tested.
Embedding uses matrix row offsets, not calendar labels.
Endogenous lag embedding and exogenous matrix join are distinct input roles.
Optional stationarity rejection checks companion eigenvalues and has no explicit iteration bound in this loop.
Companion construction transposes row-stacked coefficients after slicing deterministic terms.
IRFs use recursive Cholesky or long-run restrictions; the numerical factor is not an independently justified bank shock.
Forecast draws optionally add innovations; only endogenous lag slots advance, holding external entries fixed.
TVP IRF selects one coefficient time slice and holds it across response horizons.
bsvars: bsvars R interfaces and C++ structural temporal kernels
Development version and GPL>=3 declaration; imported scholarly references are not independently admitted here.
Holder and genuine GPL3 license text.
R constructor rejects NA but uses positional lags, a constant and optional exogenous columns.
Wrapper constructs next-origin regressors and can reset horizon from supplied conditions or exogenous paths.
IRFs include horizon zero and optionally divide impact columns by their own diagonal impacts.
Sign normalization enumerates sign combinations relative to a benchmark; it is not new identifying evidence.
Conditional forecast uses Gaussian conditioning and a Schur complement, not an intervention operator.
Stored forecast_cov is per-step innovation covariance conditional on the sampled path and draw.
Selected exception branches break horizon loops without returning a failure mask; regressor update appends the old tail beginning at N.
Native build flags and BLAS/LAPACK are part of artifact qualification.
bssm: bssm R interface and C++ state-space kernels
Package identity, GPL>=2 declaration and RcppArmadillo/sitmo dependencies; no theorem imported from description.
Univariate Gaussian constructor validates through named delegates and stores a time-series wrapper.
Selected initial covariance validator checks numeric type and dimensions, not a general PSD proof.
Native Gaussian constructors use a fixed default innovation threshold.
Likelihood skips measurement contribution when observation is nonfinite or innovation variance fails threshold; transition still runs.
Filter retains process-noise propagation on missing or low-variance branches; Joseph-style covariance on accepted updates.
PSD helper removes effectively zero diagonal directions and Cholesky-factors the remainder; it is not a general rank-revealing PSD factorization.
Reproducibility spans R posterior subsampling and the explicit C++ seed; importance weights retained by selected wrapper.
Gaussian prediction dispatch reaches the inspected univariate kernel.
State and conditional-mean predictions include sampled state dynamics; response predictions additionally include measurement noise.
panelvar: Dazhong Wu panelvar C++ kernels and Python interface
Root MIT license and named holder; dependency rights remain separate.
Python version module reports5.2.0; distinguish it from CMake project0.1.0.
Build uses architecture-specific flags and fixed Python/Eigen paths; no portable ABI demonstrated.
Observed time labels become category positions; sort result is discarded and dense mask assignment preserves incoming value order.
Native lag table is initialized to NaN and copies row lags only when the current same-variable value is non-NaN.
Inverse helper unconditionally uses complete-orthogonal-decomposition pseudoinverse.
Core computes first and second GMM steps; coefficient solve also uses the pseudoinverse helper.
Requested output step and second-step Hansen diagnostic are separate choices in selected path.
Hansen p-value uses chi-square CDF; the stored critical_value field is fed a density at0.95 rather than a quantile.
Residual covariance, orthogonalized and generalized response branches use distinct row-oriented conventions.
Wrapper classifies models using stability and Hansen thresholds; this is not independent causal validation.
